references.text: Moses fled from Pharaoh after he had killed the Egyptian. This is the background for Eliezer's name—God saved Moses from Pharaoh's sword.
Jacob blesses Joseph and refers to 'your father's God' as a helper—the same expression Moses uses regarding his child's name.
Moses describes God as Israel's help and shield, the same theme of God as helper found in Eliezer's name.
David praises God as his rock and deliverer who saves him from enemies—a parallel to Moses' confession of salvation from Pharaoh's sword.
The psalmist declares that the Lord is Israel's help and shield—the same theology of God as helper underlying the name Eliezer.
David praises God for saving His servant from the evil sword—a direct parallel to Moses' experience with Pharaoh's sword.
The author quotes from the Psalms about the Lord as helper, so that we should not fear people—the same trust in God's help that Moses expresses.
Parallel between naming as a testimony of God's deliverance in a foreign land.
Direct narrative connection: Jethro's praise confirms Moses' testimony regarding the same act of deliverance.
Theological parallel: Both testify to God as personal deliverer from death and sword.
Narrative link: Moses' role as rescuer for Jethro (2:19) contrasts with and complements his testimony about being saved by God (18:4).
